newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tapis OSP under review after buyers' forum-traders.
newsitem.headline: Tapis OSP under review after buyers' forum-traders.

text.p: Malaysia's state-owned oil firm Petronas is to review spot market Tapis crude pricing following a meeting with term contract customers last week, traders said on Tuesday.
The company has agreed to look at the official selling price (OSP) of Tapis and its relationship to other Malaysian crudes, Miri and Labuan, traders said.
However, it has not indicated if the review will result in any changes, they said.
The forum in Kuala Lumpur is hosted by Petronas every six months to hear the view of term buyers.
At this year's meeting, buyers said they were concerned that the retroactive monthly OSP for Tapis set by Petronas was often higher than the prices that had been quoted by price reporting services.
This reduced the attraction of buying Malaysian grades on a term basis, they said.
For instance, Petronas set its Tapis term price at $21.30 per barrel for liftings in May.
But the average May Tapis price quoted by Reuters -- which is used by Petronas to help set its OSPs -- was $21.18.
Petronas set its April Tapis OSP at $21.23, compared to Reuters' average Tapis spot price of $21.08.
"The OSP is always higher than the absolute levels on the spot market," said a South Korean refiner who buys Malaysian crudes on term.
Petronas sets its OSP using an average of spot quotations from two daily reporting services and then adds a premium.
The OSPs of the other Malaysian crudes are then set at a fixed differential against Tapis.
Spot Tapis, however, is normally traded using the Asia Petroleum Price Index (APPI) weekly panel submissions as a benchmark.

Traders said most reporting services already take into account the Tapis spot market premium over the APPI. That meant that Petronas term price was effectively adding another premium. Buyers said they would also like to see increased liquidity of spot Tapis to help price transparency.
"There should be more spot cargoes so that there will be greater transparency in the market," said one term buyer.
Currently, three Tapis cargoes of around 500,000 barrels each are traded monthly on the spot market.
Buyers were also unhappy that Petronas adjusted Miri's term price to Tapis OSP +10 cents per barrel in January, from Tapis OSP -10 last year.
Most buyers said they considered Miri to be a lower quality crude compared to Tapis and asked for a reduction in the differential.
"It will take a few weeks for us to review the OSPs and the differential between the grades. Then we'll decide if any adjustments will be made," said a Petronas official.
Malaysia produces 650,000 b/d of light sweet crudes, more than half of which is Tapis.
Petronas' term sales are for a basket of Malaysian crudes, the main buyers being Thailand, Taiwan, South Korea, India and some Japanese refiners.

"Tapis is the Far East benchmark and will continue to be the benchmark for as long as the markets want it. Our role is to provide transparency in the pricing," Hassan Marican, president and chief executive of Petronas said to reporters on the sidelines of an oil conference in Kuala Lumpur last week.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3301)
